title: Combined Stress Analysis of an Offset Industrial Actuator Support Bracket
studentDocumentTitle: Student Homework Questions - Offset Industrial Actuator Support Bracket
instructorDocumentTitle: Instructor Answers - Offset Industrial Actuator Support Bracket
summary: An eccentric-loading problem integrating section-cut equilibrium, rectangular-section properties, axial and bending stress superposition, transverse shear, stress elements, and critical-point assessment.
idealizedImageAlt: Instructor reference idealization of an offset actuator bracket with horizontal force F, vertical force P, offsets e, h, and c, rectangular section dimensions b and t, and surface points A and B.
problemStatement:
An offset steel bracket connects a horizontal actuator or linkage to an overhead machine frame and also supports a vertical tooling or restraint load. At the lower joint, horizontal force F and vertical force P act eccentrically relative to the centroidal axis of the vertical leg.

Use the portion below section a-a to determine the internal resultants and nominal stress state at surface points A and B. Then identify the point with the larger absolute normal stress and state the limitations of the simplified model.
engineeringGoal: Combine section-cut equilibrium, rectangular-section properties, axial stress, flexure stress, and transverse-shear behavior to characterize the local nominal stress state at section a-a.
